answers.l: HTTPS. HTTP/3 uses it too, over UDP.
SSH. Tatu Ylönen asked IANA for it in 1995 because it sat between FTP (21) and Telnet (23).
FTP control. Data travels on a second connection, which is why firewalls hate FTP.
SMTP. Most residential ISPs block it outbound to slow spam.
DNS. UDP for most queries, TCP for large answers and zone transfers.
The classic "HTTP, but not as root" port.
Default for Rails, Grafana, and a thousand Express tutorials.
Redis. Antirez chose it because it spells MERZ on a phone keypad, after showgirl Alessia Merz.
Python's http.server default, and Django's runserver.
Flask's default. Since macOS Monterey, the AirPlay receiver wants it too.
VNC display :0. Display :1 is 5901, and so on.
NTP. Its monlist command made it a favorite DDoS amplifier.
SNMP. "Simple" is doing a lot of work in that name.
DHCP server. The client listens on 68.
DHCP client. The server listens on 67.
SMB. The door EternalBlue walked through.
Mail submission: the port mail clients should actually send on.
TFTP. How network devices fetch boot images over PXE.
memcached. In 2018, exposed UDP memcached servers amplified a 1.35 Tbps DDoS against GitHub.
Docker daemon without TLS. Exposing it hands out root.
Multicast DNS. How your laptop finds the printer.
BGP. Holds the internet together, mostly on trust.
"Leet." Unofficial, and a favorite for demos.
Source engine and Steam game servers.
The git:// protocol. Unauthenticated by design. GitHub turned it off in 2022.
Reserved. Binding to port 0 asks the OS to pick any free port.
Echo. Sends back whatever you send it.
Daytime. Replies with the time as human-readable text.
Chargen. Streams characters forever; later a DDoS amplifier.
Finger. Showed who was logged in and their .plan. The Morris worm exploited fingerd.
Ident. Lets a server ask who owns your connection. IRC servers still ask.
rpcbind, the portmapper. Points clients at NFS and other RPC services.
IKE, the key exchange behind IPsec VPNs.
STUN and TURN, which help video calls get through NAT.
EPMD, the Erlang Port Mapper Daemon.
CouchDB. Its whole API is plain HTTP.
